title_problem: Catalyst palladium has to come out of the drug
p_problem: Most new small-molecule drugs are built with palladium catalysts. The rules cap palladium in the finished drug at 10 ppm, so every batch runs through scavenger beads, often twice.
title_solution: We design a ligand that grips palladium and leaves the drug alone
timeline_goal: palladium below 10 ppm in one pass on a real API stream
steps: Make the top ligands, graft on silica
Spike-and-strip tests, ICP-MS
One-pass run on a CDMO batch

title_problem: Trace nitrite turns finished drugs into nitrosamines
p_problem: Nitrite sits at ppm levels in common excipients and slowly nitrosates the drug on the shelf. The FDA has recalled or withdrawn whole drug classes over it, and limits for drug-specific nitrosamines came into force in August 2025.
market_title: Nitrosamine control: a $0.4B a year problem for US generics
title_solution: We design a scavenger that takes the nitrite before the drug does
timeline_goal: nitrosamine growth stopped in a real tablet on accelerated storage
steps: Make the top scavengers
Nitrosation race against the drug, LC-MS
Accelerated storage in a real tablet

title_problem: Antibody cells need iron, and iron falls out of the media
p_problem: Chemically defined media feed cells iron as ferric citrate, which precipitates above pH 7, or as transferrin, a plasma protein that costs more than the rest of the media. Serum-free media alone was a $2.1B market in 2025.
market_title: Cell culture media: $3.9B in 2025, over half serum-free
title_solution: We design an iron carrier that stays dissolved and still feeds the cell
timeline_goal: CHO cells at higher antibody titer than ferric citrate media
steps: Make the top carriers, load with iron
Solubility and release tests at pH 7.2
CHO shake-flask titer vs ferric citrate

title_problem: Peptide drugs come out of synthesis as TFA salts
p_problem: Peptides are purified with trifluoroacetic acid and arrive as the TFA salt. An API has to be under 1% TFA, so makers run repeated exchange passes that cost yield and time.
market_title: Counter-ion exchange: a $0.2B step in peptide making
title_solution: We design a trap that pulls TFA out and leaves acetate behind
timeline_goal: under 1% TFA in one pass on a real peptide batch
steps: Make the top traps, pack columns
TFA against acetate and chloride, ion analysis
One-pass swap on a CDMO peptide

title_problem: Bacterial debris has to come out of protein drugs
p_problem: Endotoxin from the bacteria used to make proteins causes fever at tiny doses. Columns today carry polymyxin B, an antibiotic, and lose capacity after about five cycles.
market_title: Endotoxin removal: a $0.2B market in resins and kits
title_solution: We design a binder that grips the endotoxin headgroup, not the protein
timeline_goal: endotoxin cleared from a real protein solution with full protein recovery
steps: Make the top binders, graft on resin
LAL clearance and protein recovery
Cycle life against a polymyxin column

title_problem: Drugs come as two mirror forms and one is useless
p_problem: About half of small-molecule drugs are chiral, and the two mirror forms have to be separated and measured on every batch. The columns that do it are coated with cellulose from wood pulp.
market_title: Chiral columns: $130M in 2025, plus phases and services
options: Picked for the drug up front
title_solution: We design a selector that holds one mirror form harder than the other
timeline_goal: a packed column separating a real drug's two mirror forms
steps: Make the top selectors, bond to silica
Resolution tests on model drugs
Side-by-side with a cellulose column

title_problem: Cell therapies are frozen in DMSO, which damages cells
p_problem: Freezing mixes are 10% DMSO. It kills part of the dose on thaw and has to be washed out before infusion. DMSO-free media were a $143M market in 2025 and growing 12% a year.
title_solution: We design a molecule that sits on the ice face and keeps crystals small
timeline_goal: cell survival after thaw matching 10% DMSO, with no DMSO
steps: Make the top ice blockers
Ice growth and thaw viability tests
Side-by-side with CryoStor on real cells

title_problem: Protein A is the most expensive litre in antibody making
p_problem: Every monoclonal antibody is captured on protein A resin. The resin lists at $8,000–14,000 a litre and adds $5–15 to every gram of antibody, and the protein ligand itself leaches and needs a pH 3 elution that aggregates the drug.
market_title: Protein A resin: a $1.1–1.5B market in 2025
title_solution: We design a small ligand that grips the antibody's Fc patch and lets go at mild pH
timeline_goal: one-pass capture of IgG from CHO harvest, eluted above pH 5
steps: Make the top ligands, graft on agarose
Breakthrough and elution on CHO harvest
Purity and leachate by ELISA and LC-MS

title_problem: Half of freeze-dried vaccine doses are thrown away
p_problem: WHO puts yearly waste at about half of lyophilised doses and a quarter of liquid doses, mostly from cold-chain breaks. Today's stabilisers are sugars that still need 2–8 °C, so the freezer travels with the vial.
market_title: Vaccine stabilisers: $102M in 2025 inside a $5.3B excipient market
title_solution: We design an excipient that sits where water sits on the protein, so the vial survives warm shipping
timeline_goal: a model antigen keeps potency for 4 weeks at 40 °C
steps: Make the top stabilisers, injection grade
Freeze-dry a model antigen, measure Tg
4 weeks at 40 °C, potency by ELISA
